sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: We start today with an account of two communities.
sentences.zh: 今天我们从两个社区的故事开始。

sentences.en: One is liberal.
sentences.zh: 一个是自由派的。

sentences.en: The other, conservative.
sentences.zh: 另一个是保守派的。

sentences.en: I want you to guess which is which.
sentences.zh: 我想请你猜猜哪个是哪个。

sentences.en: The schools would stress patriotism and respect,
sentences.zh: 那里的学校会强调爱国主义和尊师重道，

sentences.en: and it would be a very rules-based educational system.
sentences.zh: 而且会是一个非常注重规则的教育系统。

sentences.en: The houses would be fairly similar.
sentences.zh: 房屋会相当相似。

sentences.en: The lawns would be very nicely kept and beautifully green and mowed.
sentences.zh: 草坪会打理得非常整洁、郁郁葱葱且修剪得当。

sentences.en: The town would be quiet with lots of churches.
sentences.zh: 小镇会很安静，有许多教堂。

sentences.en: That's town one.
sentences.zh: 那是第一个小镇。

sentences.en: Here's town two.
sentences.zh: 这是第二个小镇。

sentences.en: The schools would be based more on experiential kinds of things
sentences.zh: 那里的学校会更多地基于体验式的事物，

sentences.en: rather than rope memory.
sentences.zh: 而不是死记硬背。

sentences.en: People would prefer older houses with wooden floors
sentences.zh: 人们会更喜欢铺着木地板的老房子，

sentences.en: rather than wall-to-wall carpeting.
sentences.zh: 而不是通铺地毯。

sentences.en: They would keep the yards natural.
sentences.zh: 他们会保持院子的自然状态。

sentences.en: Lots of bars and community theaters and foreign films,
sentences.zh: 有很多酒吧、社区剧院和外国电影，

sentences.en: more of those than churches.
sentences.zh: 这些比教堂还要多。

sentences.en: That was easy, right?
sentences.zh: 这很简单，对吧？

sentences.en: Conservatives lack order.
sentences.zh: 保守派缺乏秩序。

sentences.en: Liberals embrace ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 自由派拥抱模棱两可。

sentences.en: Now, you may be rolling your eyes or even getting angry at these stereotypes,
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会对这些刻板印象翻白眼甚至感到生气，

sentences.en: but we all know there's more than a grain of truth to them.
sentences.zh: 但我们都知道这里面包含着不止一点真相。

sentences.en: So how did these two towns, which our guest today refers to as Liberalville
sentences.zh: 那么这两个小镇——我们的今日嘉宾将其称为自由村

sentences.en: and Conservatine, get this way?
sentences.zh: 和保守村——是怎么变成这样的呢？

sentences.en: When most of us think about how we came to our political views,
sentences.zh: 当大多数人思考我们的政治观点是如何形成的时，

sentences.en: we tend to have a straightforward explanation.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会有一个直截了当的解释。

sentences.en: We use our upbringing and life experiences as the basis for our political beliefs.
sentences.zh: 我们以我们的成长经历和生活经验作为政治信仰的基础。

sentences.en: We imagine that our parents, teachers, and friends shape our views on everything
sentences.zh: 我们想象我们的父母、老师和朋友塑造了我们对一切事物的看法，

sentences.en: from taxes and the economy to immigration and national security.
sentences.zh: 从税收和经济到移民和国家安全。

sentences.en: But what if I told you there is something deeper to those attitudes?
sentences.zh: 但如果我告诉你，这些态度背后还有更深层次的东西呢？

sentences.en: Drives that shape the music we listen to, the food we eat, the politicians we elect.
sentences.zh: 那些塑造我们所听的音乐、所吃的食物、所选举的政治家的驱动力。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, how the partisan divide in our country
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》将探讨我们国家的党派分歧

sentences.en: might arise not just from our upbringing and lived experiences, but from biology.
sentences.zh: 可能不仅源于我们的成长和生活经验，还源于生物学。

sentences.en: On a regular basis, right before an election, someone will share an article with me
sentences.zh: 经常地，就在选举前夕，会有人跟我分享一篇文章，

sentences.en: about how science proves that the brains of liberals are stunted.
sentences.zh: 讲的是科学如何证明自由派的大脑发育不全。

sentences.en: Or a post on Twitter will say, Republicans are less intelligent than Democrats.
sentences.zh: 或者推特上的一条帖子会说，共和党人不如民主党人聪明。

sentences.en: These claims obscure something far more interesting and far more accurate.
sentences.zh: 这些说法掩盖了一些远为有趣、也远为准确的东西。

sentences.en: There are genuine psychological differences between liberals and conservatives.
sentences.zh: 自由派和保守派之间存在着真正的心理差异。

sentences.en: Understanding these differences can give us fresh insight into our political conflicts.
sentences.zh: 理解这些差异可以让我们对政治冲突有全新的认识。

sentences.en: John Hibbing is a political scientist at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 约翰·希宾是内布拉斯加大学林肯分校的政治学教授。

sentences.en: He has spent many years studying the psychological and neurological differences
sentences.zh: 他花了多年时间研究自由派和保守派之间的

sentences.en: between liberals and conservatives.
sentences.zh: 心理和神经学差异。

sentences.en: He is co-author of the book, Predisposed, Liberals, Conservatives, and the Biology of Political Differences.
sentences.zh: 他是《倾向：自由派、保守派与政治分歧的生物学》一书的合著者。

sentences.en: John, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 约翰，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you, Shanankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Pleasure to be with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起。

sentences.en: When most of us think about how we came to our political views, John,
sentences.zh: 约翰，当大多数人思考我们的政治观点是如何形成的时，

sentences.en: we have a relatively straightforward explanation that has to do with our upbringing and background.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个相对直截了当的解释，这与我们的成长和背景有关。

sentences.en: How does that theory go?
sentences.zh: 那个理论是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Well, whenever I ask my students where their political views come from,
sentences.zh: 嗯，每当我问学生他们的政治观点来自哪里时，

sentences.en: the first thing I say is their parents.
sentences.zh: 我首先说的就是他们的父母。

sentences.en: And I think we have this sense that those views that our parents have passed along
sentences.zh: 我想我们有一种感觉，即父母传给我们的这些观点，

sentences.en: are supplemented by those, you know, from a clergy member or a trusted relative, a close friend.
sentences.zh: 会得到神职人员、受信任的亲戚或亲密朋友的补充。

sentences.en: But we sort those through our own view of the world,
sentences.zh: 但我们会通过自己对世界的看法来梳理这些，

sentences.en: and we come to a very rational understanding of the world
sentences.zh: 然后我们对世界产生非常理性的理解，

sentences.en: and an understanding of what social policies are best to make the world better.
sentences.zh: 并理解什么样的社会政策最能让世界变得更好。

sentences.en: So we're going to look in depth at some of the psychological and brain differences that do exist between liberals and conservatives.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将深入探讨自由派和保守派之间确实存在的某些心理和大脑差异。

sentences.en: But I want to start by looking at how differences between partisans are not limited to politics.
sentences.zh: 但我首先想探讨的是，党派之间的差异并不仅限于政治。

sentences.en: These differences show up in many domains that have nothing to do with politics.
sentences.zh: 这些差异表现在许多与政治毫无关系的领域。

sentences.en: Republican President George H.W.
sentences.zh: 共和党总统老布什

sentences.en: Bush once spoke about an issue that had bothered him for many years.
sentences.zh: 曾谈到一个困扰了他多年的问题。

sentences.en: I do not like broccoli.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢西兰花。

sentences.en: And I haven't liked it since I was a little kid.
sentences.zh: 我从小时候起就不喜欢它。

sentences.en: And my mother made me eat it.
sentences.zh: 我母亲逼我吃它。

sentences.en: And I'm President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 而我是美国总统。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to eat any more broccoli.
sentences.zh: 我再也不会吃任何西兰花了。

sentences.en: What do food differences tell us about liberals and conservatives?
sentences.zh: 食物上的差异对我们了解自由派和保守派有什么启示？

sentences.en: Well, we tend to see that there are differences in tastes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们往往会发现品味上存在差异。

sentences.en: Conservatives do like meat and potatoes more.
sentences.zh: 保守派确实更喜欢肉类和土豆。

sentences.en: Liberals are more likely to prefer ethnic food.
sentences.zh: 自由派更有可能偏爱异国风味的食物。

sentences.en: So you see that, and that we think is part of a deeper pattern.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到这一点，而且我们认为这是更深层模式的一部分。

sentences.en: Conservatives are a little bit fonder of kind of predictability, of standard kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 保守派稍微更喜欢可预测性、标准化的事物。

sentences.en: And liberals are a little bit more willing to experiment.
sentences.zh: 而自由派则更愿意进行尝试。

sentences.en: And this comes through in food, taste, and a variety of other things.
sentences.zh: 这一点体现在食物、品味以及各种其他事物中。

sentences.en: Here's another example.
sentences.zh: 这里有另一个例子。

sentences.en: Researchers once went into the living spaces of people, offices and dorm rooms, and they recorded the items that they saw.
sentences.zh: 研究人员曾走进人们的生活空间（办公室和宿舍），并记录了他们看到的物品。

sentences.en: What was different about the living and workspaces of liberals and conservatives?
sentences.zh: 自由派和保守派的生活和工作空间有什么不同？

sentences.en: Well, conservatives tended to have lots of things like sports memorabilia, whereas liberals tended to have more experiential things, lots of books, lots of CDs,
sentences.zh: 嗯，保守派往往有很多诸如体育纪念品之类的小物件，而自由派往往有更多体验式的东西，比如很多书、很多CD，

sentences.en: especially diverse CDs,
sentences.zh: 特别是风格多样的CD，

sentences.en: whereas conservatives were more likely to have things that organized their lives, calendars, clothes baskets.
sentences.zh: 而保守派更有可能拥有组织他们生活的东西，比如日历、洗衣篮。

sentences.en: Also, the researchers suggested the liberals' rooms were not quite as tidy or as well-lighted as the conservative rooms and offices.
sentences.zh: 此外，研究人员指出，自由派的房间不如保守派的房间和办公室那么整洁或明亮。

sentences.en: There's even been some research looking at differences in our preferences for different kinds of pets.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一些研究探讨了我们对不同种类宠物的偏好差异。

sentences.en: I understand Jonathan Haidt and others have explored that liberals and conservatives gravitate at different kinds of dogs.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，乔纳森·海特和其他人曾探讨过自由派和保守派倾向于不同种类的狗。

sentences.en: Different kinds of dogs.
sentences.zh: 不同种类的狗。

sentences.en: It tends to be the case that conservatives prefer purebreds, and liberals will go with mixed-breed dogs.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，保守派更喜欢纯种狗，而自由派则会选择混血狗。

sentences.en: There are some studies that suggest how you view pets.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究表明了你如何看待宠物。

sentences.en: There isn't that much difference in how many have pets.
sentences.zh: 养宠物的人数比例并没有太大差异。

sentences.en: Both liberals and conservatives like to have pets at about equal level, but they might view them somewhat differently.
sentences.zh: 自由派和保守派喜欢养宠物的程度差不多，但他们看待宠物的方式可能有些不同。

sentences.en: Liberals are a little bit more likely to view them as part of the family rather than, you know, just a pet.
sentences.zh: 自由派稍微更有可能把它们视为家庭成员，而不仅仅是，你知道的，一只宠物。

sentences.en: And so you have those kinds of very interesting things, not just in pet ownership, but kind of in orientation to the pet.
sentences.zh: 所以你会发现这些非常有趣的事情，不仅在宠物所有权方面，还在于对宠物的定位。

sentences.en: The patterns that John and others have identified are more than just curious.
sentences.zh: 约翰和他人发现的这些模式不仅仅是好奇心使然。

sentences.en: These patterns suggest that our model of political differences is wrong in an important way.
sentences.zh: 这些模式表明，我们在政治分歧上的模型在一个重要方面是错误的。

sentences.en: Liberals and conservatives don't just have different political preferences.
sentences.zh: 自由派和保守派不仅有不同的政治偏好。

sentences.en: They have different temperaments.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的气质。

sentences.en: Conservatives don't just care about lower taxes.
sentences.zh: 保守派不仅关心更低的税收。

sentences.en: They also care about where the poetry rhymes.
sentences.zh: 他们也关心诗歌是否押韵。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Should poetry rhyme?
sentences.zh: 诗歌应该押韵吗？

sentences.en: We also ask, you know, are you more comfortable with novels that end with clear resolution?
sentences.zh: 我们还会问，你知道的，你是否对以清晰结局收尾的小说感到更舒适？

sentences.en: Those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can start to see a pattern already, I think, in our discussion that it is the case that liberals are more likely to say, sure, I'm okay with free verse.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我想你在我们的讨论中已经开始看出一种模式了，那就是自由派更有可能会说，当然，我能接受自由诗。

sentences.en: Whereas conservatives say, no, you know, we really think there should be a pattern.
sentences.zh: 而保守派则会说，不，你知道的，我们真的认为应该有一种模式。

sentences.en: Music should come back to a recognizable melody.
sentences.zh: 音乐应该回归到可辨认的旋律。

sentences.en: Poetry should rhyme.
sentences.zh: 诗歌应该押韵。

sentences.en: And novels should wrap up in a way that we are comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 小说应该以让我们感到舒适的方式收尾。

sentences.en: To be clear, the differences John identifies are averages.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，约翰指出的差异是平均值。

sentences.en: So you can certainly have a Republican who likes free verse and a Democrat who hates jazz.
sentences.zh: 所以你完全可以遇到一个喜欢自由诗的共和党人，和一个讨厌爵士乐的民主党人。

sentences.en: The point of this research isn't to stereotype liberals and conservatives, but to show that our political choices flow from deeply ingrained psychological differences.
sentences.zh: 这项研究的目的不是给自由派和保守派贴上刻板印象，而是表明我们的政治选择源于根深蒂固的心理差异。

sentences.en: Many of us don't realize how our choices as consumers, the cars we buy, the food we eat, the music we listen to, that these choices inadvertently reveal our political preferences.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人没有意识到，我们作为消费者的选择、我们购买的汽车、我们吃的食物、我们听的音乐，这些选择无意中暴露了我们的政治偏好。

sentences.en: So I'm happy to tell people on Facebook what kind of music I listen to, but I imagine that they wouldn't be able to tell from that whether I was a Democrat or a Republican.
sentences.zh: 所以我很乐意在脸书上告诉人们我听什么类型的音乐，但我猜他们无法从中看出我是民主党人还是共和党人。

sentences.en: I asked John about research that suggests you can tell whether someone's a conservative or a liberal if you know what kind of movies they watch, what kind of food they eat,
sentences.zh: 我问约翰关于这样一项研究：如果你知道一个人看什么类型的电影、吃什么类型的食物，

sentences.en: what kind of vacations they take.
sentences.zh: 他们进行什么类型的假期，你就能看出他是保守派还是自由派。

sentences.en: It's very reasonable that people would not resonate with that line of argument because to them, it's not like they say, well, you know, in order to be a good conservative,
sentences.zh: 人们对这种论点产生共鸣是很合理的，因为对他们来说，这不像是他们会说，好吧，你知道的，为了成为一个好的保守派，

sentences.en: I need to do this or in order to be a good liberal.
sentences.zh: 我需要这样做，或者为了成为一个好的自由派。

sentences.en: So, you know, they're just being themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他们只是在做自己。

sentences.en: And I think that's the real message here is that our political beliefs are part and parcel of our entire being.
sentences.zh: 我想这才是真正的核心信息，即我们的政治信仰是我们整个生命中不可分割的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, it's not like they're completely separate.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不像是它们是完全独立的。

sentences.en: And it's just a natural outgrowth of these larger psychological and even physiological tendencies that we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们一直在谈论的这些更广泛的心理甚至生理倾向的自然延伸。

sentences.en: When we come back, the psychological traits and brain differences that shape our political choices and preferences.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨塑造我们政治选择和偏好的心理特质与大脑差异。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请不要走开。

sentences.en: I want to start with one of the most important differences you and others have identified when it comes to politics.
sentences.zh: 我想从你和他人识别出的关于政治的最重要差异之一开始。

sentences.en: Liberals and conservatives differ when it comes to how they see threats and danger.
sentences.zh: 自由派和保守派在看待威胁和危险的方式上存在差异。

sentences.en: Here's Wayne LaPierre of the National Rifle Association.
sentences.zh: 这是全国步枪协会的韦恩·拉皮埃尔。

sentences.en: We know in the world that surrounds us, there are terrorists and there are home invaders, drug cartels, carjackers, knockout gamers and rapers and haters and campus killers,
sentences.zh: 我们知道在我们周围的世界里，有恐怖分子，有入室抢劫犯、贩毒集团、劫车犯、随机袭击者、强奸犯、仇恨者以及校园杀手，

sentences.en: airport killers, shopping mall killers.
sentences.zh: 机场杀手、购物中心杀手。

sentences.en: So talk about this difference, John.
sentences.zh: 所以谈谈这种差异吧，约翰。

sentences.en: John, when liberals hear this, what do they hear?
sentences.zh: 约翰，当自由派听到这个时，他们听到了什么？

sentences.en: When conservatives hear this, what do they hear?
sentences.zh: 当保守派听到这个时，他们听到了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is a remarkable quote.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是一段引人注目的引言。

sentences.en: I remember John Stewart played this once on The Daily Show and after the clip, they panned back to Stewart.
sentences.zh: 我记得乔恩·斯图尔特曾在《每日秀》上播放过这个，在片段播放完后，镜头切回了斯图尔特。

sentences.en: Where the s*** do you live?
sentences.zh: 你他妈住在哪儿啊？

sentences.en: And he was hiding behind his desk.
sentences.zh: 他正躲在他的办公桌后面。

sentences.en: So, you know, you get the sense that if you listen to this very long, you're scared of everything.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你会有一种感觉，如果你听这个太久，你会对一切都感到害怕。

sentences.en: The message that I take from this is that, you know, you play this to liberals and they say, this guy's nuts.
sentences.zh: 我从中得到的讯息是，你知道的，你把这个放给自由派听，他们会说，这家伙疯了。

sentences.en: You know, others have told me he's just doing it because he makes millions of dollars from the NRA and he doesn't really believe it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，其他人告诉我，他这么做只是因为他从全国步枪协会赚了数百万美元，他并不是真的相信这一点。

sentences.en: I think he does.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是相信的。

sentences.en: These threats are very real to him and we're not going to get anywhere unless people who don't feel that way understand that some people do.
sentences.zh: 这些威胁对他来说非常真实，如果我们不让那些没有这种感受的人理解确实有人有这种感受，我们将一事无成。

sentences.en: And likewise, the Wayne LaPierres of the world need to understand that for some people, they just, you know, they don't see the world as threatening as he does.
sentences.zh: 同样地，世上的韦恩·拉皮埃尔们也需要明白，对某些人来说，他们只是，你知道的，他们不像他那样觉得世界充满威胁。

sentences.en: And they don't think we need to build our society around mitigating those threats.
sentences.zh: 他们也不认为我们需要围绕减轻这些威胁来构建我们的社会。

sentences.en: So, you know, when a liberal like John Stewart hides behind the desk, partly what he's doing is he's mocking Wayne LaPierre, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当像乔恩·斯图尔特这样的自由派躲在办公桌后面时，他部分的行为是在嘲笑韦恩·拉皮埃尔，对吧？

sentences.en: He's sort of saying, this is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 他有点像在说，这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: It's beyond ridiculous to imagine that all these threats are basically around us.
sentences.zh: 想象所有这些威胁基本上就在我们身边，这简直荒谬至极。

sentences.en: We live in a relatively safe society.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个相对安全的社会里。

sentences.en: And basically, what John Stewart is communicating is, you know, what you're saying doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 基本上，乔恩·斯图尔特想要传达的是，你知道的，你所说的话没有任何意义。

sentences.en: And what you're saying is, it might not make sense to you, but it makes sense to Wayne LaPierre.
sentences.zh: 而你所说的是，它对你来说可能没有意义，但对韦恩·拉皮埃尔来说是有意义的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: You know, one of the favorite things for conservatives to say about liberals is that they just don't get it, meaning that, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，保守派最喜欢用来评价自由派的一句话就是他们根本不懂，这意味着，你知道的，

sentences.en: they don't appreciate that it's a dangerous world.
sentences.zh: 他们没有意识到这是一个充满危险的世界。

sentences.en: And I think that is absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是真实的。

sentences.en: But it's not that they don't get it because they're being obtuse or they're not informed.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是因为他们愚钝或孤陋寡闻才不理解。

sentences.en: They read about events in the world and they just don't respond to them in the same way.
sentences.zh: 他们阅读世界各地发生的事情，只是不会以相同的方式作出反应。

sentences.en: And likewise, liberals rather need to recognize that while this may seem silly, and you're right about John Stewart mocking this, you know, how can you, you know,
sentences.zh: 同样地，自由派也需要认识到，虽然这看起来很傻，而且你嘲笑乔恩·斯图尔特模仿这个是对的，你知道，你怎么能，你知道，

sentences.en: live your life worried and whatever.
sentences.zh: 整天担惊受怕地过日子。

sentences.en: But to them, this is very real.
sentences.zh: 但对他们来说，这是非常真实的感觉。

sentences.en: And a good citizen is vigilant and is prepared to do battle to protect himself, his family, and society from those threats.
sentences.zh: 一个优秀的公民是高度警惕的，并随时准备战斗，以保护自己、家人和社会的免受这些威胁。

sentences.en: What's interesting about both groups here is that there is a very powerful illusion that we have that the rest of the world sees the world the way that we see the world.
sentences.zh: 这两类人群最有趣的地方在于，我们有一种非常强烈的错觉，认为世界上其他人看待世界的方式和我们是一样的。

sentences.en: And if they come to a different conclusion, it must be because they're being deliberately obtuse or somehow deliberately biased,
sentences.zh: 如果他们得出不同的结论，那一定是因为他们故意装傻或抱有某种故意的偏见，

sentences.en: as opposed to the idea that people are actually, they might be seeing the world the same way, but their reactions to the world might actually be very different.
sentences.zh: 而不是说人们实际上可能看待世界的方式是一样的，但他们对世界的反应实际上可能截然不同。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm really glad you brought that up.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很高兴你提出这一点。

sentences.en: Psychologists talk about false consensus.
sentences.zh: 心理学家称之为虚假共识效应。

sentences.en: So it turns out that if your favorite color is blue, you grossly overstate the percent of the population whose favorite color is blue.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，如果你最喜欢的颜色是蓝色，你就会大大高估人口中喜欢蓝色的人的比例。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think we need to recognize that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为我们需要认识到这一点。

sentences.en: We did a study once.
sentences.zh: 我们曾经做过一项研究。

sentences.en: There's a substance, androstenone.
sentences.zh: 有一种物质叫雄甾烯酮。

sentences.en: It turns out that people smell it very differently.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，人们对它的气味反应非常不同。

sentences.en: It's just because our olfactory systems are structured differently.
sentences.zh: 这只是因为我们的嗅觉系统结构不同。

sentences.en: Some people smell it very favorably.
sentences.zh: 有些人闻起来觉得很好闻。

sentences.en: It smells like kind of cookies or incense.
sentences.zh: 闻起来有点像曲奇饼干或熏香。

sentences.en: Others smell it unfavorably.
sentences.zh: 其他人闻起来觉得很难闻。

sentences.en: It'll smell like sweat or even urine.
sentences.zh: 闻起来像汗水甚至尿液。

sentences.en: And some don't smell it at all.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人根本闻不到。

sentences.en: And it's a genetically based difference.
sentences.zh: 这是基于基因差异的。

sentences.en: So we had a bunch of our graduate students smell this.
sentences.zh: 所以我们让一群研究生闻了这个气味。

sentences.en: And I remember one fellow, and he smelled it, and it just smelled awful to him.
sentences.zh: 我记得有个家伙，他闻了一下，觉得这味道糟透了。

sentences.en: And it didn't smell awful to many of the other graduate students.
sentences.zh: 其他很多研究生并没有觉得这味道那么糟糕。

sentences.en: And he was convinced that this was some kind of psychological trick that we were trying to, you know, get him to say, well, yeah, it doesn't smell bad.
sentences.zh: 他深信这是一种心理把戏，我们想让他说，“好吧，是的，闻起来并不坏”。

sentences.en: It was one of those studies when, in fact, he just couldn't believe that people were that different in the way they smelled this substance.
sentences.zh: 这是那种研究，事实上，他只是无法相信人们在闻这种物质时会有如此大的差异。

sentences.en: And I think the same thing applies to political beliefs and to the way we experience threats in the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为同样的道理也适用于政治信仰以及我们体验世界威胁的方式。

sentences.en: I remember one of the things that broke the Internet recently was the big controversy about whether people heard the word laurel or heard the word yanny.
sentences.zh: 我记得最近有一件事让整个互联网炸锅了，那就是大家都在争论听到的词是“laurel”还是“yanny”。

sentences.en: But this idea that, you know, the way that we see, hear something must be the way everyone else sees it.
sentences.zh: 但这种观点认为，你知道，我们看到、听到某事的方式，一定也是其他人看到它的方式。

sentences.en: And there's just this feeling of utter disbelief that other people might not see and hear the world the same way.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种彻底的不信任感，觉得别人看世界和听世界的方式可能跟自己不一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's just what we're used to.
sentences.zh: 是的，这只是我们习惯了而已。

sentences.en: It makes sense to us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说很合逻辑。

sentences.en: So I do think that's something we need to continue to pound away on, that we really are wired up quite differently.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为这是我们需要持续强调的一点，那就是我们的生理机制确实截然不同。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's look at how this plays out when it comes to the subject of immigration.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，让我们来看看这在移民问题上是如何体现的。

sentences.en: Here is Republican Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这里是共和党人唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: They're bringing drugs.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了毒品。

sentences.en: They're bringing crime.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了犯罪。

sentences.en: They're rapists.
sentences.zh: 他们是强奸犯。

sentences.en: And some, I assume, are good people.
sentences.zh: 我猜其中有些人是好人。

sentences.en: And here is Democrat Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 这里是民主党人南希·佩洛西。

sentences.en: We are constantly reinvigorated by immigrants coming to our country.
sentences.zh: 来到我们国家的移民源源不断地为我们注入新的活力。

sentences.en: Their commitment and courage and commitment to the American dream, which drew them here in the first place, strengthens the American dream.
sentences.zh: 他们对最初吸引他们来这里的美国梦的执着、勇气和奉献，进一步巩固了美国梦。

sentences.en: Now, it's important to stipulate here, John, that it's entirely possible these are politicians.
sentences.zh: 现在，约翰，这里有必要说明一下，完全有可能是因为他们是政客。

sentences.en: They might indeed be saying things that are just politically strategic.
sentences.zh: 他们说的话可能确实只出于政治策略的考量。

sentences.en: But how might differences in threat perception shape the way liberals and conservatives in general think about the subject of immigration?
sentences.zh: 但是，威胁感知能力的差异又将如何塑造自由派和保守派总体上对移民问题的看法呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I really think, you know, immigration, defense, police, law and order.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的认为，你知道，移民、国防、警察、法律与秩序。

sentences.en: I think this is really at the core of who we are and at the core of political differences.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的是我们核心本质的体现，也是政治分歧的核心所在。

sentences.en: So, you know, if I am a person like Wayne LaPierre who feels these threats and thinks they're all around us,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果我是一个像韦恩·拉皮埃尔那样能够感受到这些威胁并且认为它们无处不在的人，

sentences.en: then it seems to me I would want a set of policies put forward by our government that helped to reduce those threats.
sentences.zh: 那么在我看来，我会希望政府出台一套政策来帮助减少这些威胁。

sentences.en: And how am I going to do this?
sentences.zh: 我将如何做到这一点？

sentences.en: I'm going to do it by allowing people to be well armed.
sentences.zh: 我将通过允许人们充分武装自己来实现这一点。

sentences.en: I'm going to do it by spending a lot on defense.
sentences.zh: 我将通过在国防上投入巨资来实现这一点。

sentences.en: I'm going to empower police.
sentences.zh: 我将赋予警察更多的权力。

sentences.en: I'm going to have the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 我将保留死刑。

sentences.en: I'm going to not allow immigrants to come here.
sentences.zh: 我将不允许移民来到这里。

sentences.en: Or if they do, they're going to be extremely vetted, as the president once said.
sentences.zh: 或者如果他们来了，正如总统曾经说过的，他们将接受极其严格的审查。

sentences.en: So, you know, those, I think, to a threat-sensitive mindset are steps that, you know, they only make sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，对那些对威胁敏感的心态来说，这些是顺理成章的步骤。

sentences.en: They just can't really understand why anybody would be opposed to those kinds of things because this would help us to be a safer place.
sentences.zh: 他们只是真的无法理解为什么会有人反对这类事情，因为这能帮我们创造一个更安全的地方。

sentences.en: Now, there are all kinds of confounding factors when it comes to studying how politicians speak in the actual world,
sentences.zh: 现在，在研究政客在现实世界中如何发言时，存在着各种各样的混杂因素，

sentences.en: political considerations that are difficult to disentangle from psychological and biological traits.
sentences.zh: 有些政治考量很难与心理和生理特征分离开来。

sentences.en: But John and others have studied these differences in experimental settings.
sentences.zh: 但约翰和其他人在实验环境中研究了这些差异。

sentences.en: John once showed liberals and conservatives positive and negative pictures, and he found they reacted very differently.
sentences.zh: 约翰曾经向自由派和保守派展示过积极和消极的图片，他发现他们的反应截然不同。

sentences.en: A positive picture would be something like a beautiful sunset or somebody enjoying themselves on a ski slope, a happy child.
sentences.zh: 积极的图片可能是美丽的日落、某人在滑雪道上享受乐趣，或者一个快乐的孩子。

sentences.en: A negative picture would be things like a house that had just been leveled by a hurricane or a guy eating worms or children who are malnourished.
sentences.zh: 消极的图片可能是被飓风夷为平地的房屋、吃虫子的男人或者营养不良的儿童。

sentences.en: We had people hooked up to some physiological devices.
sentences.zh: 我们给参与者连接了一些生理设备。

sentences.en: The most obvious one is electrodermal activity or skin conductance, which is a common way of seeing if somebody is just having a reaction,
sentences.zh: 最明显的是皮电活动或皮肤电导，这是观察某人是否有反应的常用方法，

sentences.en: having a physiological arousal to that stimulus.
sentences.zh: 对该刺激产生生理唤醒反应。

sentences.en: And what we found is that people do have arousals when they see these kinds of images because they have some emotional content.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当人们看到这类图像时确实会产生唤醒反应，因为它们包含某种情感内容。

sentences.en: But we tended to find that liberals were more reactive to the positive images and conservatives are more reactive to the negative images.
sentences.zh: 但我们倾向于发现，自由派对积极图像的反应更强烈，而保守派对消极图像的反应更强烈。

sentences.en: I understand that in one brain imaging study that you conducted, volunteers were shown disgusting images,
sentences.zh: 据我所知，在你主持的一项脑成像研究中，志愿者被展示了令人恶心的图片，

sentences.en: and brain activation from even a single image was actually pretty good at being able to tell who was liberal and who was conservative.
sentences.zh: 仅凭单张图片的脑部激活情况，其实就能很好地辨别出谁是自由派，谁是保守派。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: There have been three or four studies that attempt to see if the brain activation patterns of liberals and conservatives is different.
sentences.zh: 已经有三四项研究试图观察自由派和保守派的大脑激活模式是否不同。

sentences.en: And the one that we did goes back to kind of our favorite thing, which is to show them these different kinds of pictures.
sentences.zh: 我们做的那项研究可以追溯到我们最喜欢的事情，也就是向他们展示这些不同类型的图片。

sentences.en: Actually, we had the most luck with pictures of mutilations.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们在展示肢体残缺的图片时效果最好。

sentences.en: And you're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: When we did that, it was very easy to categorize people without knowing anything about them.
sentences.zh: 当我们这样做时，在对人们一无所知的情况下，可以非常轻松地对他们进行分类。

sentences.en: All we would look at was the brain scan results.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要查看脑部扫描结果。

sentences.en: And we could be incredibly accurate knowing whether they're liberal or conservative just on the basis of that.
sentences.zh: 仅凭这一点，我们就能以极其准确的方式知道他们是自由派还是保守派。

sentences.en: Liberals' brains, when they looked at mutilation images, were much more active in a part of the brain called the S2, somatosensory 2.
sentences.zh: 当自由派看到肢体残缺的图片时，他们大脑中被称为S2（第二体感皮层）的区域会更加活跃。

sentences.en: And this is part of the brain that will be activated if you suffer pain.
sentences.zh: 这是大脑中在你遭受痛苦时会被激活的一部分。

sentences.en: So if I kick you in the shin, your somatosensory 2 would be active.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我踢你的小腿迎面骨，你的第二体感皮层就会被激活。

sentences.en: But it's also active if you see pain in others.
sentences.zh: 但当你看到别人痛苦时，它也会被激活。

sentences.en: And so if you would see a movie of somebody stepping on a rusty nail, it goes right through their foot.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你看到有人踩到生锈铁钉并穿透脚掌的电影片段，

sentences.en: Your somatosensory 2 would be active.
sentences.zh: 你的第二体感皮层就会被激活。

sentences.en: And what we saw in these brain scans was that liberals were more likely to have activation in somatosensory 2 than conservatives.
sentences.zh: 我们在这些脑部扫描中看到的是，自由派比保守派更有可能在第二体感皮层产生激活。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that conservatives are hard-hearted.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着保守派铁石心肠。

sentences.en: It just means that things are happening differently when they see these different images.
sentences.zh: 这只是意味着当他们看到这些不同的图像时，大脑的处理过程有所不同。

sentences.en: Now you could argue that a lot of this research is correlational.
sentences.zh: 现在你可能会争辩说，很多这样的研究都只是相关性的。

sentences.en: You could also argue that a lot of the patterns that John and others find are consistent with the power of upbringing in shaping political preferences.
sentences.zh: 你还可以争辩说，约翰和其他人发现的许多模式都与后天教养在塑造政治偏好方面的强大作用相一致。

sentences.en: Here's how.
sentences.zh: 具体是这样的。

sentences.en: Let's say I'm raised in a conservative home.
sentences.zh: 假设我在一个保守的家庭中长大。

sentences.en: I learned to be politically conservative from my parents.
sentences.zh: 我从父母那里学会了政治上保持保守。

sentences.en: But my family also influences all kinds of other things about me that have nothing to do with politics.
sentences.zh: 但我的家庭也影响了我的各种其他方面，而这些与政治毫无关系。

sentences.en: They shape the kind of food I like to eat, the kind of movies I like to watch, the kind of sports I enjoy.
sentences.zh: 他们塑造了我喜欢吃什么食物，喜欢看什么电影，喜欢什么运动。

sentences.en: By this line of reasoning, the fact that liberals and conservatives are different on all manner of things isn't about biology.
sentences.zh: 按照这种逻辑，自由派和保守派在方方面面都有所不同，这并不是因为生物学原因。

sentences.en: It just shows you how your family environment can affect lots of things about you.
sentences.zh: 这只是向你展示了家庭环境如何影响你身上的许多方面。

sentences.en: There's a really interesting way to separate the effects of biology from the environment.
sentences.zh: 有一种非常有趣的方法可以将生物学的影响与环境的影响分离开来。

sentences.en: Think about fraternal and identical twins.
sentences.zh: 想想异卵双胞胎和同卵双胞胎。

sentences.en: Identical twins have identical genes.
sentences.zh: 同卵双胞胎拥有相同的基因。

sentences.en: Fraternal twins have similar but not identical genes.
sentences.zh: 异卵双胞胎拥有相似但不相同的基因。

sentences.en: If you follow a group of fraternal and identical twins, each twin pair is raised in the same household.
sentences.zh: 如果你追踪一组异卵双胞胎和同卵双胞胎，每一对双胞胎都在同一个家庭中长大。

sentences.en: Each pair eats the same food, listens to the same conversations, watches the same movies.
sentences.zh: 每一对都吃同样的食物，听同样的对话，看同样的电影。

sentences.en: Now, if you find differences between identical twins as a group and fraternal twins as a group,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你发现同卵双胞胎群体与异卵双胞胎群体之间存在差异，

sentences.en: that suggests that biology, not environment, is the driver.
sentences.zh: 这就表明是生物学因素，而不是环境因素在起主导作用。

sentences.en: I asked John what such studies reveal about political preferences.
sentences.zh: 我问约翰，这类研究揭示了关于政治偏好的什么信息。

sentences.en: We were fortunate to have access to a data set that's very large and includes thousands and thousands of twin pairs
sentences.zh: 我们很幸运能够访问一个非常庞大的数据集，其中包含成千上万对双胞胎，

sentences.en: collected by a guy named Lyndon Eves long ago.
sentences.zh: 这是很久以前一个叫林登·伊夫斯的人收集的。

sentences.en: It's a fairly dated data set.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当陈旧的数据集。

sentences.en: But it was a valuable one for us because it included lots of information about their political views.
sentences.zh: 但对我们来说它很有价值，因为它包含了大量关于他们政治观点的信息。

sentences.en: And when we subjected these data to the standard twin design approach,
sentences.zh: 当我们把这些数据提交给标准的双胞胎设计方法进行分析时，

sentences.en: we did indeed find that their political views were quite heritable.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现他们的政治观点具有相当高的遗传性。

sentences.en: Although people oftentimes misread this,
sentences.zh: 尽管人们经常误解这一点，

sentences.en: our results suggested that maybe 30 or 40 percent of our political views come from genetics.
sentences.zh: 但我们的结果表明，也许我们30%或40%的政治观点来自于遗传。

sentences.en: But, you know, that bothered a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这困扰了很多人。

sentences.en: And this was quite a controversial study in political science.
sentences.zh: 这在政治学中是一项颇具争议的研究。

sentences.en: Many people didn't like that at all.
sentences.zh: 许多人非常不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And they tended to over-interpret those results
sentences.zh: 他们往往过度解读这些结果，

sentences.en: and make it sound like we were saying that everything was genetic.
sentences.zh: 说得好像我们在断言一切都是由基因决定的一样。

sentences.en: But, you know, if it's 34 percent genetic, that obviously leaves, you know, 50, 60, 70 percent that comes from the environment.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果34%是遗传的，显然还剩下50%、60%、70%来自于环境。

sentences.en: So all we're saying is that that genetic component is not zero.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要说的只是遗传成分并非为零。

sentences.en: But apparently that was enough that some people were upset about that.
sentences.zh: 但显然这已经足够让一些人感到不安了。

sentences.en: And so you basically, you're able to tell in some ways that there is a closer link in the political orientation of identical twins
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你在某种程度上能够看出同卵双胞胎的政治倾向之间存在更紧密的联系，

sentences.en: than in the political orientation of fraternal twins.
sentences.zh: 而异卵双胞胎则没有那么紧密。

sentences.en: And that tells you that there is some element of the biology, some element of genetics that is driving political preferences.
sentences.zh: 这告诉你，生物学的某些因素，遗传的某些因素正在驱动着政治偏好。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: No, that's well put.
sentences.zh: 不，这话讲得很对。

sentences.en: And again, it's nice to compare political views with other kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，将政治观点与其他类型的事物进行比较是一件很有意思的事。

sentences.en: Height, for example, turns out to be about 80 percent heritable when you see these, you know,
sentences.zh: 例如，当你进行这种研究时，你会发现身高大约有80%的遗传率，你知道，

sentences.en: when you subject it to the same kind of design.
sentences.zh: 当你对它采用同类型的设计时。

sentences.en: Personality traits are about 50 to 60 percent.
sentences.zh: 人格特质大约占50%到60%。

sentences.en: Political views, 30 to 40 percent, I would say.
sentences.zh: 至于政治观点，我认为大约占30%到40%。

sentences.en: One of the big implications of all of this work, besides just being interesting in itself,
sentences.zh: 所有这些工作带来的重大意义之一，除了其本身的趣味性之外，

sentences.en: is that it helps us, I think, think about the political conflicts we have with fresh insight.
sentences.zh: 我认为，它有助于我们以全新的视角来思考我们所经历的政治冲突。

sentences.en: And you've made the case that in many ways, the more we're able to see the differences between groups of people as inherent or biological,
sentences.zh: 你曾提出过这样的观点：在很多情况下，我们越是把人群之间的差异视为内在的或生物学的，

sentences.en: in some ways it changes the way we think about those differences.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它就会改变我们对这些差异的看法。

sentences.en: Talk to me about that idea, John.
sentences.zh: 约翰，跟我谈谈这个想法吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: When other traits have been understood to be biological, I'm thinking of something like handedness.
sentences.zh: 当其他特征被理解为生物学特性时，我想到了诸如用惯左手还是右手之类的事情。

sentences.en: You know, we used to think that if you were left-handed, that was just because you got into a lazy habit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们过去认为如果你是左撇子，那只是因为你染上了懒惰的习惯。

sentences.en: My father was left-handed, and the teacher, you know, this was long ago,
sentences.zh: 我父亲是个左撇子，老师，你知道，那是很久以前的事了，

sentences.en: would beat him on the hand with a ruler whenever he wrote with his left hand,
sentences.zh: 每当他用左手写字时，就会用直尺打他的手，

sentences.en: trained him to write with his right hand.
sentences.zh: 训练他用右手写字。

sentences.en: So we viewed that as a flaw, something that needed to be driven out.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把这视为一种缺陷，一种需要被根除的东西。

sentences.en: Of course, now we understand that being left-handed is very biological.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在我们明白左撇子是非常纯粹的生物学现象。

sentences.en: This is something much deeper than just a lazy habit.
sentences.zh: 这远比单纯的懒习惯要深得多。

sentences.en: Or, of course, you know, the big one today would be sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道的，如今最大的一个例子就是性取向。

sentences.en: When people realize that sexual orientation is indeed biologically driven
sentences.zh: 当人们意识到性取向确实是由生物学驱动的，

sentences.en: and not something that they just have decided to do,
sentences.zh: 而不是他们自己随随便便决定要这样的，

sentences.en: then people are much more tolerant of that.
sentences.zh: 人们对这方面的容忍度就会高得多。

sentences.en: So we were wondering if perhaps the same thing might happen with regard to politics,
sentences.zh: 所以我们在想，政治上或许也会发生同样的情况，

sentences.en: if we realize that our political opponents were not simply being lazy,
sentences.zh: 如果我们意识到我们的政治对手不只是在偷懒，

sentences.en: but rather were oriented to the world in a different fashion,
sentences.zh: 而是以一种不同的方式来看待世界，

sentences.en: that maybe we would be a little bit more tolerant of them,
sentences.zh: 也许我们对他们的容忍度就会稍微高一点，

sentences.en: that this is the only way we're going to get anywhere,
sentences.zh: 如果我们至少能理解他们的立场，

sentences.en: if we at least understand where they're coming from,
sentences.zh: 这才是我们能够取得进展的唯一途径，

sentences.en: even if we still might deeply disagree with their conclusions.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们可能依然极其不赞同他们的结论。

sentences.en: What would you say to critics who would say,
sentences.zh: 你会对那些批评者说些什么呢？

sentences.en: you know, the argument that psychological traits and biological differences
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种认为心理特征和生物学差异

sentences.en: are beneath our deep political conflicts doesn't make sense
sentences.zh: 并不是我们深层政治冲突根源的观点是说不通的，

sentences.en: because we didn't always have this deep divide in our country
sentences.zh: 因为我们国家过去并没有一直存在这种深沟高垒的对立，

sentences.en: between liberals and conservatives.
sentences.zh: 也就是自由派和保守派之间的对立。

sentences.en: There was a time when we had many, many more people in the center.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，我们有非常非常多的人处于政治中间派。

sentences.en: The most liberal Republican was often to the left of the most conservative Democrat.
sentences.zh: 最开明的共和党人往往比最保守的民主党人还要偏左。

sentences.en: And, you know, there really has been a sorting of the political parties in recent years.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，近年来政党确实经历了一次阵营重组。

sentences.en: What explains this change, especially over the last 20, 30 years?
sentences.zh: 是什么解释了这种变化，尤其是过去二三十年来的变化？

sentences.en: What I would say to that argument is that I believe we have always had this very same division,
sentences.zh: 我对这种论点的回应是，我相信我们其实一直都存在着这种相同的分歧，

sentences.en: this very basic difference between people who are fairly sensitive to threats
sentences.zh: 也就是那些对威胁相当敏感、

sentences.en: and think we need to be vigilant,
sentences.zh: 认为我们需要保持警惕的人，

sentences.en: and those people who are more into experimentation and trying new things.
sentences.zh: 与那些更热衷于进行实验和尝试新事物的人之间这种最基本的差异。

sentences.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson has a great quote.
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生有一句很棒的名言。

sentences.en: I'm sorry I can't give it to you verbatim,
sentences.zh: 很抱歉我不能一字不差地背诵出来，

sentences.en: but it's basically that the division between those people who are supporters of tradition
sentences.zh: 但大意是：支持传统的人

sentences.en: and those people who are supportive of innovation is very old
sentences.zh: 与支持革新的人之间的分歧由来已久，

sentences.en: and has structured the world since time began.
sentences.zh: 并且自开天辟地以来就构建了整个世界。

sentences.en: John Hibbing is a political scientist at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 约翰·希宾是内布拉斯加大学林肯分校的政治学教授。

sentences.en: He has spent years studying the psychological and neurological differences
sentences.zh: 他多年来一直致力于研究自由派和保守派之间的

sentences.en: between liberals and conservatives.
sentences.zh: 心理学和神经学差异。

sentences.en: Along with Kevin Smith and John Alford,
sentences.zh: 他和凯文·史密斯以及约翰·阿尔福德一起，

sentences.en: he's the co-author of the book,
sentences.zh: 合著了一本书，

sentences.en: Predisposed, Liberals, Conservatives, and the Biology of Political Differences.
sentences.zh: 书名为《基因决定：自由派、保守派与政治分歧的生物学基础》。

sentences.zh: 约翰，谢谢你今天来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.zh: 由塔拉·博伊尔和卡米拉·瓦尔加斯-雷斯特雷波剪辑。

sentences.zh: 我们的团队包括雷娜·科恩、珍妮·施密特、帕思·沙阿和劳拉·奎雷尔。

sentences.zh: 亚历克斯在NPR的IT团队工作。

sentences.zh: 他最近帮我们更新了归档系统。

sentences.zh: 在整个过程中，

sentences.zh: 这是一项浩大的工程，

sentences.zh: 涉及了一百多期“隐藏的大脑”节目，
